text: Remember that goods can often be related to each other in various ways when it comes to demand and price changes! Think about how these relationships might affect consumer behavior as prices fluctuate. Keep exploring different types of connections between products; you're on the right track by considering their interactions with market dynamics.

Consider how goods are related in terms of consumer purchasing behavior when prices change and think about what happens to demand for products that go together. Reflect on options B (complementary relationship) as it directly relates to a decrease in price leading to an increase in the quantity demanded of another good used with it.

When you observe an increase in demand for one product as its price decreases and it's known to be used together with another item, this indicates a specific type of relationship between goods that are often consumed or used together. Think about how these products interact when their prices change relative to each other.
